acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc:
Ira tells the story of two friends who had this incredible power to save someone. And with that great power came great responsibility.
Jane and Glen are with Mission USA, working with gang kids in Chicago's prisons.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc:
Alex Kotlowitz reports on a woman with the power to change two people's lives — and at the height of her power, she doesn't even know she has it.
Alex is the author of Never a City So Real and other books.
acts.title: Objects In Side View Mirror Are Truer Than They Appear

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Ira Glass talks with a mother and daughter who spent years watching their neighbor do things they found shocking and felt powerless to stop. Then, suddenly, they get the power to decisively change things permanently. And they have to decide if they will.
acts.title: Unwelcome Wagon

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc:
When you're powerless, you spend a lot of time thinking about the people above you — what they want, why they do what they do, whether they'll ever come through. Shalom Auslander has a story about that relationship.
This story is from Shalom's collection, Beware of God.
acts.title: Waiting For Joe
